Color becomes sound.

Chromaflow is an ambient instrument and a living fluid canvas. Droplets add dye and momentum to an incompressible fluid simulation. When they land, their horizontal position selects a note from the current chord. Each color plays a different sampled instrument. Choose a palette swatch to keep new droplets in that one color and voice, including automatic rain and blooms. Enable Cycle colors beside the palette to restore variety.

Sound is powered by WebAudioFont by Sergey Surikov, with 28 instruments from the FluidR3 GM soundfont by Frank Wen. All instrument samples and the playback engine are served with this site. The sustained voices use gentle attack envelopes and extended releases for softer, overlapping swells. Eight experimental textures add crystalline rain, soundtrack and atmosphere tones, spectral brightness, alien choruses, echoes, and sci-fi signals, with individual slow filter sweeps. Reverb uses a locally generated stereo impulse response; delay uses a filtered feedback loop synchronized to the tempo.

The fluid uses semi-Lagrangian advection, pressure projection, and vorticity confinement. Your settings stay in this browser. No account or server-side storage is needed for the instrument.

A rhythm beneath the color

The optional Rhythm tab adds four percussion voices and a sixteen-step beat studio. Start with a groove, edit hits and accents, or generate evenly spaced patterns and rotate them into new rhythms. Ten percussion sounds are synthesized locally with Web Audio, with swing, humanize, and independent levels. Percussion has its own reverb and delay amounts. Voices and drums share one echo-spacing setting, available in Sound, Rhythm, and Beat studio. Both delay lines follow the effective percussion tempo, including half/double speed, with eighth-note, dotted-eighth, and quarter-note echoes. Their timed hits create visible ripples, add momentum to the existing fluid, or both. No new dye or melodic notes are added by percussion.

Play with your whole hand

The Perform tab explains six gestures. Position shapes pitch, stereo placement, weight, tone, and length. Slow strokes make soft ribbons; quick strokes and flicks create short accents and jets. Circles make whirlpools and stereo motion. Hold still, then release a bloom of long chord tones. Vertical sweeps conduct a filter across the entire composition, which gently settles after release. Gesture intensity, a whole-scene toggle, and a reset let you choose the amount of expression.
